summary: Checked 6 claims against Google's official help pages and Nango's Google review guide. Core path and timelines held up; one cost claim was misattributed to Google and two documented nuances were missing.

corrections.claim: Restricted Gmail scopes require a security assessment that is redone every year
corrections.finding: Confirmed. Google: 'applications requesting access to restricted scopes must undergo an annual security assessment… All applications must be revalidated every year.'

corrections.claim: In Testing status, refresh tokens expire after 7 days
corrections.finding: Confirmed, except when only name/email/profile scopes are requested.
Consistent: Google publishes '4-6 weeks' for restricted scope reviews; Nango reports 5-20 days for well-prepared teams, with CASA usually the longer leg. Kept as reported.
Google's Security Assessment page states the requirement but no price. Figures come from vendors (Nango, Aug 2025: ~$700 Netsentries, $3,000+ Prescient). Re-attributed as vendor-reported.
Since January 2026 users can grant a subset of requested scopes; apps must handle partial grants. Added as a blocker.
Google documents a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per client ID; the oldest is silently revoked. Added to technical notes.
